sentences.text:
This Writ Appeal Having Come Up For Admission On
15-09-2017, The Court On The Same Day Delivered The Following:
 Navaniti Prasad Singh, C.J. & Raja Vijayaraghavan V., J.

- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
 Dated this the 15th day of September, 2017
 Judgment
Navaniti Prasad Singh, C.J.
The Commissioner of Food Safety is in appeal against an interim order dated 24.07.2017 passed by learned single Judge of this Court in W.P.(C) No.22698 of 2017.
We have heard the learned Additional Advocate General and the learned counsel appearing for the respondent/writ petitioner and with their consent we are deciding this appeal at this stage itself.
2. It appears that the respondent/writ petitioner had imported large quantity of wheat.
It operates a modern Roller Flour Mill.
Substantial quantity of wheat on arrival at Cochin was lifted and taken away.
About 15,000 metric tonnes of wheat was left at the Cochin Port warehouse.
Pursuant to some press reports, the Food Safety authorities conducted a search and took samples of the stored wheat.
Their report indicated that wheat had become unfit for human consumption.
They accordingly passed orders under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (for short 'the Act, 2006') seizing the entire quantity of wheat at the warehouse in Cochin Port.
The writ petitioner moved this Court.

3. The writ petitioner's submission before the learned single Judge was that the wheat, if properly washed and processed, could be made fit for human consumption and therefore, fit for the use by the petitioner.
They wanted a chance to be given by the Food Safety authorities to do so, as the contamination as reported were mainly damaged grains and high urea content.
The learned single Judge passed an interim order in respect of 20 metric tonnes only, out of the 15,000 metric tonnes.

The learned single Judge directed the Food authorities to ensure that the 20 metric tonnes were removed from the warehouse to the flour mill of the writ petitioner, cleaned and washed under their supervision and then the stocks were to be sealed and samples taken.
These samples were then to be tested whether it was now fit for human consumption or not.
The reports were to be submitted to the Court.
It is this order against which the Commissioner of Food Safety has approached this Court.
4. Learned Additional Advocate General appearing for the appellant submits that such a procedure is not envisaged under the Act, 2006.
We have gone through the Act.
In our view, Section 18(1)(f) of the Act, 2006 gives an indication thereof.
We may note that there are basically two types of unsafe food articles.
The first type would comprise of items which have become inherently unsafe and has to be destroyed.
It cannot be permitted to be used.

The second type are those which may have The Commissioner Of Food Safety vs Peekay Roller Flour Mills on 24 July, 2017 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84577797/
2 removable contamination.

sentences.text: It cannot be permitted to be marketed unless such contamination is removed.
The Act does not say that any contamination that could be removed cannot be permitted to be removed.
The risk of contaminated food entering the market has to be controlled absolutely and if contamination can be removed, that would amount to elimination of the risk.

We, therefore,
find nothing wrong in the order of the learned single Judge.
Holding otherwise would be a waste where 15000 metric tonnes of wheat which could otherwise be cleaned and used would have to be necessarily destroyed.
Surely that is not contemplated.

5. We may note that once the Commissioner of Food Safety filed this appeal, it appears that they did not cooperate in implementing the earlier orders of learned single Judge and subsequently the learned single Judge modified the order on 30.08.2017 by appointing an Advocate Commissioner.

It was directed that the 20 metric tonnes of wheat lying at the warehouse in the Cochin Port would be removed, transported, cleaned and processed at the writ petitioner's flour mill and the Advocate Commissioner was ordered to supervise the same.
Once it was so done, then it was left to the Food Safety Commissioner to get it tested again.
We think that this was not proper.
6. The learned single Judge ought to have directed the Food Safety authorities to supervise this process to obviate any undesirable practice which could have been adopted by the Mill.
We must keep in mind that we are dealing with food safety aspect and there cannot be any leniency in such matters.
We, therefore, find no reason to interfere and accordingly dismiss this appeal.

But while doing so, we would direct the authorities to ensure that no part of the stocks which have been processed will be allowed to be sold without proper sampling and testing and only if it is certified fit for human consumption, the same would be permitted to be used.
Further consignments would also be allowed to be moved, if the first consignment is found to be fit for human use.

But, even those consignments would be moved under the supervision of Food Safety Officers, and they would be processed and cleaned under the strict vigilance of the Food Safety Officers and after proper sampling, analysis report is to be obtained certifying that the so processed and cleaned wheat is fit for human consumption and only then the writ petitioner will be allowed to use it in any manner.

If the reports are otherwise, then the authorities would direct the writ petitioner to take delivery of the entire stock and ensure its destruction so that there is no chance of the contaminated food item finding its way into the market in one way or the other.

We may also observe that it would be open to the Commissioner for Food Safety to raise demand by way of compensation for the additional supervision costs being incurred by the Department which supervision inures to the benefit of the flour mill.
The flour mill will be obliged to pay any such reasonable amount as may be demanded in this regard by the Commissioner of Food Safety.
We make it clear that no part of the stocks would be processed and/or sold unless it is certified by the authorities to be fit for human consumption.
The appeal is accordingly dismissed.
It is expected that the Commissioner would co-operate in the matter and ensure that there is no further delay in the matter.

Sd/-
Navaniti Prasad Singh, Chief Justice.
